+=== Accesses that overlap in time
+The second part of R3 looks for two threads that use the same exchange at the same time, as KCSAN does in the Linux
+kernel. The routing engine uses an exchange at known points: a step is called, the callback of a step continues the
+exchange, and an on completion runs. At a sample of these points the thread opens a short watch window on the exchange
+and pauses in it. If another thread comes to a point of the same exchange during the window, both are reported.
+Each report names the thread and its stack (`USED_BY_TWO_THREADS`). A thread that only waits, such as a caller that waits
+for its task, is at no point, so it is not reported. The return of `process` is not a point: after an asynchronous
+processor handed the exchange on, its caller only unwinds, while the thread that got the exchange may already call the
+callback. An access between these points is not seen. Examples are an `AggregationStrategy` that runs on a thread of
+a pool, `copyResults` after a circuit breaker timed out, and a thread of the application that reads the headers. The
+rule finds overlaps at the points of the routing engine, not every overlap.
+The sample is taken by a counter, not at random: `camel.sanitizer.overlapSampling=100` opens a window at every 100th
+point of the context. When one thread routes the exchanges, a rerun samples the same points. When several threads do,
+they share the counter, and it falls on other points from run to run. A window pauses its thread for
+`camel.sanitizer.overlapWindow` (`1ms` by default). The pause uses the system clock, not the `TimeSource` of the
+context, so a virtual clock of camel-test-dst does not stretch it.
+The pause makes a rare overlap more likely, which is the point, but it changes the timing of the application, and a
+paused I/O thread (such as a Netty event loop) serves nothing else while it waits. So the sampling is off by default,
+also with profile `dev`, and on at 1 in 100 points in a test (`@CamelSanitizer`, or the CI switch). A test that fails
+only because of the pauses (a short timeout, a throttler) fails with its own assertion, not with a report of the
+sanitizer, so the two can be told apart. Such a test class turns the sampling off for itself with
+`@CamelSanitizer(overlapSampling = 0)`. With the sampling off nothing is installed for it, so it costs nothing.
+The windows are kept by the id of the exchange and hold no exchange. A copy that keeps the id of its exchange (the
+copies of a `loop` with `copy`, or an exchange that a transport in the same JVM rebuilds with the id of the sender, as
+`transferExchange` does) is another exchange: the windows tell the two apart by their identity hash, so they are not
+reported together. Two threads that both continue an exchange because of a violation already reported for it (a
+callback called twice, a callback after a throw, a return value that differs from the value of the callback, a commit
+run twice) overlap because of that violation, so the overlap is not reported again. An overlap with another cause in
+the same exchange is not reported either, but the exchange already has its report. An exchange gets at most one report
+of an overlap.
+A report of an overlap looks like this:
+[source,text]
+Exchange sanitizer: exchange used by two threads at the same time (R3)
+  exchange 5A1B...-0000000000000003, route orders, step handOff, processor com.acme.AuditHandOff
+  watched while the callback of step handOff of route orders continues the exchange: thread Camel (camel-1) thread #3 - timer://orders
+      at com.acme.AuditHandOff.process(AuditHandOff.java:41)
+  meanwhile step audit1 of route audit is called: thread audit-2
+      at org.apache.camel.support.StepHelper.process(StepHelper.java:63)
+      at com.acme.AuditHandOff.lambda$process$0(AuditHandOff.java:38)
+  An exchange can move between threads, but it must never be used by two threads at the same time (see AsyncProcessor).

+  Usual fix: let one thread at a time use the exchange: a processor that hands it to another thread returns false from process and leaves it to that thread (only that thread calls the callback); work that must run beside the route gets a copy of the exchange (as the wire tap does).
+Here `AuditHandOff` sends the exchange itself to the route `audit` on a thread of its own and goes on, as a wire tap
+by hand: the route and the audit route use the same exchange at the same time.

+ * Chaos and the watch windows of rule R3 of the exchange sanitizer together, with the tracer, the backlog tracer and
+ * the backlog debugger on as well: a watch window is opened at every point where the routing engine uses an exchange
+ * ({@code overlapSampling = 1}), and the chaos rules that fail, delay and duplicate steps and sends cause no report.
+ * The duplicate rule is the interesting case: the producer is called twice within one call of the step. The tests cover
+ * the three ways the two sends run:

+ *
  • the endpoint completes synchronously: the thread of the caller makes both sends;

+ *
  • the duplicated send comes after a {@code threads} EIP: a thread of the pool makes both sends;
+ * <li>the endpoint completes asynchronously: the thread that completed the first send makes the second send while the
+ * thread of the caller unwinds.
+ * The tests record the thread that makes each send, so they check which case ran.
+@CamelSanitizer(overlapSampling = 1)
+class ChaosWithSanitizerWatchWindowsTest extends ChaosTestSupport {
+    private static final Logger LOG = LoggerFactory.getLogger(ChaosWithSanitizerWatchWindowsTest.class);
+    private static final Pattern WINDOWS = Pattern.compile("(\\d+) watch windows? opened \\(R3, at 1 in 1 points\\)");
+    private final AtomicInteger work = new AtomicInteger();
+    // the threads that made the sends to direct:receiver (a direct consumer runs on the thread of the send), in order
+    private final List<Thread> receiverSenders = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
+    // the threads that made the sends to direct:pooledReceiver, in order, per exchange: the two threads of the pool
+    // can route two exchanges at once, so the sends of different exchanges can interleave
+    private final Map<String, List<Thread>> pooledSenders = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
+    private BacklogDebugger debugger;
+    @Override
+    protected CamelContext createCamelContext() throws Exception {
+        CamelContext context = super.createCamelContext();
+        context.setTracing(true);
+        context.setBacklogTracing(true);
+        context.setDebugging(true);
+        // no breakpoint is set, so the debugger never suspends an exchange
+        debugger = DefaultBacklogDebugger.createDebugger(context);
+        context.addLifecycleStrategy(new LifecycleStrategySupport() {
+            @Override
+            public void onContextStarted(CamelContext context) {
+                debugger.enableDebugger();
+        context.addService(debugger);
+        return context;
+    @Override
+    protected RouteBuilder createRouteBuilder() {
+        return new RouteBuilder() {
+            @Override
+            public void configure() {
+                from("direct:retry").routeId("retry")
+                        .errorHandler(defaultErrorHandler().maximumRedeliveries(2).redeliveryDelay(0).logStackTrace(false))
+                        .process(e -> work.incrementAndGet()).id("work")
+                        .to("mock:retry").id("toRetry");
+                // the receiver completes asynchronously: threads(1) hands the exchange to its thread, so the first
+                // send returns false, and that thread completes it and makes the second send
+                from("direct:twice").routeId("twice").to("direct:receiver").id("toReceiver");
+                from("direct:receiver").routeId("receiver")
+                        .process(e -> receiverSenders.add(Thread.currentThread())).id("receiverSender")
+                        .threads(1).id("receiverPool")
+                        .to("mock:received").id("toReceived");
+                from("direct:twiceToMock").routeId("twiceToMock").to("mock:duplicated").id("toMock");
+                // the send that chaos duplicates runs on a thread of the pool, not on the thread of the caller
+                from("direct:pooled").routeId("pooled").threads(2).id("pool").to("direct:pooledReceiver").id("toPooled");
+                from("direct:pooledReceiver").routeId("pooledReceiver")
+                        .process(e -> pooledSenders.computeIfAbsent(e.getExchangeId(), k -> new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>())
+                                .add(Thread.currentThread()))
+                        .id("pooledSender")
+                        .to("mock:pooled").id("toPooledMock");
